title: Abolitionist & Resistance Poetry: Freneau & Dunbar
author: Philip Freneau & Paul Laurence Dunbar
citation: Freneau, Philip. 'The African Chief.' 1790; Dunbar, Paul Laurence. 'We Wear the Mask.' Lyrics of Lowly Life, Dodd, Mead and Co., 1896.

sections.heading: The African Chief by Philip Freneau (1790)

epigraph.quote: He stood, a monarch in his chains, with noble mien and regal eye.

paragraphs:
See how in chains the captive stands,
Far from his native golden sands!
Though bound with iron, bold and high,
He lifts to heaven a fearless eye;
A king upon the battlefield,
Whose spirit never learned to yield;
He scorns the tyrant's whip and rod,
And bows his soul to none but God.

What crime was his, that on our shore
He bleeds, an exile evermore?
His only fault: he loved his land,
And dared against invaders stand!
Shame on the nation that can boast
Of freedom along every coast,
Yet binds in heavy, rusted chain
The brave whose freedom was their reign!

sections.heading: We Wear the Mask by Paul Laurence Dunbar (1896)

epigraph.quote: We wear the mask that grins and lies, it hides our cheeks and shades our eyes.

paragraphs:
We wear the mask that grins and lies,
It hides our cheeks and shades our eyes,—
This debt we pay to human guile;
With torn and bleeding hearts we smile,
And mouth with myriad subtleties.

Why should the world be over-wise,
In counting all our tears and sighs?
Nay, let them only see us, while
We wear the mask.

We smile, but, O great Christ, our cries
To thee from tortured souls arise.
We sing, but oh the clay is vile
Beneath our feet, and long the mile;
But let the world dream otherwise,
We wear the mask!
